title: Delete Node in a BST
summary: Given a BST's root node and a key, locate and remove the node with that key.
statement: Given a BST's root node and a key, locate and remove the node with that key. Return the updated root node. The deletion process involves two main steps: finding the node to delete and then removing it.
constraints: 0 <= node count <= 10,000; all values are unique integers between -100,000 and 100,000.
The input is a valid BST and -100,000 <= key <= 100,000. Remove key if it exists; otherwise keep all values.
Return a TreeNode root or None. Any valid BST containing exactly the remaining values is accepted; balancing is not required.

hints: Deleting a BST node has zero-child, one-child, and two-child cases.
For two children, use the inorder successor or predecessor, then unlink its old position.
Search while retaining the parent. For two children copy the successor value, then remove that successor using its right child.
Reconnect the parent to the surviving child, or return that child as the new root. Iteration handles a 10,000-node chain without recursion overflow.
editorial: The smallest value in the right subtree can replace a two-child target without breaking BST ordering. That successor has no left child, so unlinking it is a one-child operation. Retaining the parent permits root and non-root removal with constant auxiliary space. A predecessor-based solution is equally correct. The judge checks strict BST ordering and exactly the surviving integer values, not one reference shape or a balance requirement. The oracle independently filters the value set and labels a complete tree in inorder.
